# xfo-miner v1.0.8

This release promotes the approved BATCH 65 miner-side Hashcat capability probe and XMRig local log hygiene work into the formal miner release baseline.

## Highlights

- Adds miner-side dynamic Hashcat capability probe handling so the Pool can verify mode/keyspace support before assignment.
- Reports runtime Hashcat unsupported evidence back to the Pool with safe reason codes and sanitized summaries.
- Adds configurable local XMRig stdout/stderr logging with active-log rolling and narrow retention cleanup.

## Scope

### Hashcat capability probes and runtime unsupported reporting

- `internal/pool/protocol.go` now includes the Hashcat capability probe and result message contracts used by the Pool capability gate.
- `internal/scheduler/scheduler.go` validates Pool-owned probe payloads, rejects unsafe arbitrary arguments, and reports supported, unsupported, or error outcomes.
- `internal/scheduler/hashcat.go` materializes safe synthetic probe inputs for supported keyspace contracts and captures sanitized Hashcat evidence.
- `internal/scheduler/hashcat_evidence.go` centralizes safe evidence classification and summary trimming for unsupported probe/runtime outcomes.
- Regression coverage in `internal/scheduler/hashcat_probe_test.go` validates metadata-only dictionary probes, unsupported classification, unsafe argument rejection, and result payload shaping.

### XMRig configurable local log rotation

- `internal/config/config.go` adds `cpu_mining.xmrig_log_path`, defaulting enabled CPU mining to a config-directory-relative `logs/xmrig.log` while preserving absolute paths.
- `internal/scheduler/xmrig.go` redirects XMRig stdout/stderr to the configured local sink instead of flooding the main miner console.
- Active XMRig logs now roll before append if stale and roll again during long-running writes after the active-log age threshold.
- Retention cleanup only deletes miner-created rotated names shaped as `<active-base>.xfo-<unix_nano>.log`, preserving unrelated sibling files.
- Docs and sample config now describe the XMRig log path setting for operators.

## Why this release matters

- Reduces failed Hashcat assignments by letting the Pool probe real miner support before dispatch.
- Keeps unsupported Hashcat behavior queue-safe and observable without exposing raw wallet material or arbitrary probe arguments.
- Prevents long-running XMRig output from growing the main console indefinitely while avoiding unsafe deletion of unrelated operator files.

## Validation

- Verified with:
  - `go test ./internal/pool ./internal/scheduler`
  - `go test ./internal/config ./internal/scheduler`
  - `go test ./...`

## Operator notes

- Existing configs continue to work. When `cpu_mining.enabled` is true and `cpu_mining.xmrig_log_path` is omitted, the miner writes XMRig output under `logs/xmrig.log` next to the config file.
- Set `cpu_mining.xmrig_log_path` to an absolute path if you want XMRig output stored outside the config directory.
- Rotated XMRig logs are miner-owned only when they use the `.xfo-<unix_nano>.log` suffix; unrelated files in the same directory are preserved.
